title: Let the first HVA UI write draft sidecar state
decision: The first HVA UI prototype should edit draft workbook sidecar state directly, with approved workbook state remaining locked until a future review/apply workflow exists.
context: The service-backed sidecar boundary is in place. The next HVA UI step needs to feel live without bypassing the approved-history guardrails.
rationale: Draft sidecar writes let the workbook become useful immediately while protecting approved state, Git history, and audit semantics. This mirrors the broader low-ceremony draft plus explicit approval model for document edits.
alternatives_considered: Keep the first HVA UI read-only against approved sidecar state
Allow the HVA UI to write approved sidecar state directly
Use front-end-only state until the full review workflow exists
consequences: The HVA UI can save local draft workbook state through the service
Approved sidecar writes remain blocked at the generic service endpoint
Future review/apply work must promote draft sidecar state into approved sidecar state with audit and Git history
The UI must make draft versus approved state visible
